properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 4:17AM EST until November 25 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 500 AM EST.

* At 417 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 41 nm east of Floyd's Wall Northeast,
moving north at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
properties.area: Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 3:47AM EST until November 25 at 4:45AM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Craig Key to west end of Seven Mile Bridge
out 60 nm...
Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key 20 to 60 nm out...

* Until 445 AM EST.

* At 347 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm with possible waterspouts was
located 8 nm southeast of Marathon Humps, moving northeast at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Marathon Humps.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for severe thunderstorms with wind gusts in excess of 50
knots, extremely rough seas, frequent lightning, and torrential
downpours. Be advised that any severe thunderstorm can spawn a
waterspout or tornado. Stay low or go below, and make sure all on
board are wearing life jackets.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Straits of Florida from Craig Key to west end of Seven Mile Bridge out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key 20 to 60 NM out; Straits of Florida from Craig Key to west end of Seven Mile Bridge 20 to 60 NM out

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 3:26AM EST until November 25 at 6:30AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Miami-Dade County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 630 AM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 326 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Homestead, Homestead Miami Speedway, The Redland, Florida City,
Leisure City, Naranja, Homestead Base, Princeton and Goulds.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 5.7 feet.

Flood Stage, reaching 6.2 feet late this weekend. Additional
rises are possible thereafter.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:24PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 121 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue
11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
